mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the diagnostic floral characters of the Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae families?

options.A: Fabaceae flowers are typically zygomorphic with a banner, wings and keel; Solanaceae have actinomorphic pentamerous flowers with a fused corolla and superior ovary; Liliaceae possess trimerous flowers with six tepals and a superior ovary.
options.B: Fabaceae have actinomorphic flowers with fused petals; Solanaceae have zygomorphic flowers with a banner; Liliaceae have pentamerous flowers with an inferior ovary.
options.C: Fabaceae and Solanaceae both have trimerous flowers; Liliaceae have zygomorphic flowers with a keel.
options.D: All three families have actinomorphic flowers with five separate petals.

mcqs.answer: Fabaceae flowers are typically zygomorphic with a banner, wings and keel; Solanaceae have actinomorphic pentamerous flowers with a fused corolla and superior ovary; Liliaceae possess trimerous flowers with six tepals and a superior ovary.
mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae (legume family) is characterised by papilionaceous (banner‑wing‑keel) zygomorphic flowers. Solanaceae (nightshade family) shows actinomorphic, usually pentamerous flowers with a fused corolla and a superior ovary. Liliaceae (lily family) displays trimerous flowers having six tepals (three petals and three sepals that look alike) and a superior ovary. The other options mix up these distinctive traits, making them incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following lists only economically important members from the Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae families?
mcqs.explanation: Pea, soybean, lentil etc. belong to Fabaceae and are major food legumes. Potato and tomato are key crops of Solanaceae. Onion is a widely cultivated member of Liliaceae. Option A contains only genuine, economically important species from the three families. Options B, C and D either include species from other families (wheat, lily, daffodil) or mis‑assign families, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic is typical of the Fabaceae family?

options.B: Flowers with fused petals forming a tube and an inferior ovary
options.D: Flowers with numerous stamens and a superior ovary

mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae (legume family) is distinguished by papilionaceous flowers – a large upper petal (banner), two lateral petals (wings) and two lower petals fused to form a keel. This zygomorphic arrangement is a diagnostic feature. The other options describe traits of Solanaceae (fused corolla), Liliaceae (trimerous tepals), or generic monocot flowers, not Fabaceae.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the floral traits of the Solanaceae family?

options.A: Flowers are actinomorphic, usually pentamerous, with a fused corolla and a superior ovary
options.B: Flowers are zygomorphic with a banner, wings and keel
options.C: Flowers are trimerous with six tepals and a superior ovary
options.D: Flowers have a single petal and an inferior ovary

mcqs.answer: Flowers are actinomorphic, usually pentamerous, with a fused corolla and a superior ovary
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae (nightshade family) typically bears actinomorphic (radially symmetric) flowers that are pentamerous (five parts) with a tubular, fused corolla and a superior ovary. Options B and C describe Fabaceae and Liliaceae respectively, while D does not correspond to any of the three families.

mcqs.question: Which feature distinguishes the Liliaceae family from Fabaceae and Solanaceae?

options.A: Flowers are trimerous with six tepals and a superior ovary
options.B: Papilionaceous flower structure with banner, wings and keel
options.C: Actinomorphic pentamerous flowers with a fused corolla and inferior ovary
options.D: Numerous stamens arranged in two whorls

mcqs.answer: Flowers are trimerous with six tepals and a superior ovary
mcqs.explanation: Liliaceae (lily family) is characterised by trimerous flowers—three petals and three sepals that look alike (six tepals)—and a superior ovary. Fabaceae shows papilionaceous (banner‑wing‑keel) flowers, while Solanaceae has actinomorphic pentamerous flowers with a fused corolla. Option D describes typical monocot flowers but is not a unique distinguishing trait for Liliaceae.

mcqs.question: A botanist finds a flower that is actinomorphic, pentamerous, has a fused corolla and a superior ovary. To which family does it most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: The described combination—actinomorphic (radial symmetry), pentamerous parts, fused corolla, and superior ovary—is characteristic of the Solanaceae family. Fabaceae flowers are zygomorphic with a banner‑wing‑keel arrangement, Liliaceae flowers are trimerous, and Asteraceae have composite inflorescences, so they do not match the description.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches a plant with its family and a major economic use?

options.A: Soybean – Fabaceae – source of edible oil
options.B: Tomato – Fabaceae – source of edible oil
options.C: Onion – Solanaceae – source of edible oil

mcqs.answer: Soybean – Fabaceae – source of edible oil
mcqs.explanation: Soybean belongs to Fabaceae and is a major source of edible oil and protein. Tomato is a Solanaceae member, not Fabaceae, and its primary economic value is as a vegetable fruit, not oil. Onion is in Liliaceae and is used as a vegetable, not for oil. Pea is a Fabaceae legume, not Liliaceae, and is cultivated for food rather than ornamentation. Hence only option A is fully correct.

mcqs.question: A farmer observes a leguminous crop with papilionaceous flowers having a large upper petal, two lateral petals and two fused lower petals forming a keel. To which family does this plant belong?
mcqs.explanation: The described flower morphology—banner, wings, and keel—is the hallmark of papilionaceous flowers found exclusively in the Fabaceae (legume) family. Solanaceae flowers are actinomorphic with a fused corolla, Liliaceae flowers are trimerous, and Poaceae (grasses) have highly reduced, wind‑pollinated flowers. Therefore, the correct family is Fabaceae.
